clauses.reason: Executive Order 6487-B of December 9, 1933 states: "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry." That command is an approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and it has legal effect only through that approval: under section 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, and under sections 3(c) and 3(f) violations were restrainable in equity and punishable as misdemeanors. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no other effective date, so the command ended as a prospective operative command on June 14, 1935. No earlier end is shown (see earlier_end_check). The June 16, 1935 expiry is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced it with April 1, 1936. Schechter (295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date.

inventory_overrides.reason: Items 1 to 3 and the first part of item 4 are findings that command nothing, and item 4 also carries the final operative sentence. The corrected inventory is the single sentence that approves the code.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6487-B (December 9, 1933) is an approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Read in full from the held American Presidency Project transcription. Identity, date and subject agree with the census register and the WPA 1944 list (page 555, December 9, 1933). APP page check passed: the mirror page record with the held text's sha256 (common-crawl capture) has a heading naming this order's number, the same date and subject, and a text_sha256 equal to the held text's. The order's own text states no limit on the approval. Its command depends entirely on the code approval, so its first end is the repeal of the code-approval and code-enforcement provisions of Title I by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 on June 14, 1935, applying SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and its adjudication; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization only.

EO 6812 (August 4, 1934) approves an amendment and modifies the approvals made by orders dated December 9, 1933, April 20, 1934 and June 29, 1934 to include an approval of the code in its entirety as amended. EO 6945 (January 10, 1935), EO 6954 (January 31, 1935), EO 7017 (April 19, 1935) and EO 7022 (April 20, 1935) each approve amendments and modify the previous approval to include an approval of the code in its entirety as amended. None cancels, suspends, supersedes or revokes the approval. Each later order is an amendment and therefore a later event of this approval, not an end; no source-backed event record for these orders is available in this packet, so none is entered in later_events. EO 6685 and EO 6812 refer to this order by its date, not its number, and no held text cites it by number. No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or revoked before June 14, 1935, and none shows a modification under section 10(b) that reached this order's command. savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences, and the section 5 exemption from the antitrust laws for action complying with an approved code taken while Title I was in effect is likewise an accrued effect for completed action. The proviso to section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 names agreements and action under them, not codes, and states no time limit; the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the section 5 exemption for past action under codes, and whatever exemption survives for past action is an accrued effect, not continued operation of this approval. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval after June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495, held the code provisions in question invalid on both of its grounds; recorded as a validity characterization of section 3 code approvals, not as an end date for this order. It adjudicated the Live Poultry Code provisions and cancelled or withdrew no other approving order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: date the Act was approved; states the repealed legal effects of a code approval, not an end date
source_notes.reason: Sections 3(a)-(f) state the legal effects of an approved code that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed: the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition (3(b)), district courts could restrain violations (3(c)), and violations were misdemeanors (3(f)).
